newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-EMI sees music market growth at 6-8 pct.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-EMI sees music market growth at 6-8 pct.

text.p: EMI Group Plc said on Tuesday it expected the global music market to grow at a rate of between six and eight percent a year in the medium to long-term.
"What we're saying is what we said when we held roadshows prior to the (Thorn) demerger, that we expect 6-8 pct long term market growth," Finance Director Simon Duffy told Reuters.

"This year is looking a little bit below that level," added Duffy, saying that markets so far this year had been mixed but that overall first half growth had been 5.5 percent, comparable to the same period last year.

Turnover from the EMI Music division fell slightly to 1.096 billion pounds in the first half from 1.114 billion in the same period last year but improved margins helped the division lift operating profit to 131.9 million stg from 124.6 million.
Duffy said the relative strength of sterling in the first half had depressed sales figures.

The EMI finance director said that overall music sales were "virtually flat" in the U.S. and declined slightly in France. But they rebounded in Germany while growth in the UK and the rest of Europe was stronger than expected. Japan saw substantial growth and southeast Asia and Latin America saw large gains.
Shares in EMI, which demerged from Thorn Plc in August, had been under pressure in recent weeks over fears that the music market had stalled after a decade of strong growth.
They were trading 10-1/2p higher at 1281-1/2p by 0955 GMT on Tuesday.

EMI said it had a strong release schedule for the second half. But it said that in contrast to last year releases were more weighted towards its fourth quarter rather than the important pre-Christmas period.
The third quarter has on some occasions accounted for as much as 40 percent of annual sales.
Duffy said that the release schedule was dependent on when artists produced recordings.

EMI is pinning its third quarter hopes on the third and final Beatles Anthology album, which entered the U.S. charts at number one, a triple album from the Artist Formerly Known as Prince and the debut album from UK newcomers the Spice Girls.
Expected fourth quarter offerings include releases from Robbie Williams, Blur, Simple Minds, Megadeth and Jon Secada.

Duffy would not disclose how much EMI had paid for the one-off Prince project, saying only it was a "sensible amount" for both parties. He said that more Prince recordings could follow if things went well.
